alsoKnownAs.name: Parmesan
alsoKnownAs.note: Inside the EU the name is reserved to Parmigiano-Reggiano; elsewhere it is used loosely for any hard grating cheese.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Grana Padano
notToBeConfusedWith.note: A separate protected cheese made across a far larger area of northern Italy, aged for less time and milder for it. It is not the vegetarian alternative it is sometimes taken for — its own production standard also requires calf rennet.

forms.label: Aged, made with animal rennet
forms.sourceNote: USDA publishes no record for the protected designation; this is its record for hard parmesan. Its grated-parmesan record carries a measured density but nearly 14 g of carbohydrate per 100 g, which describes a shelf-stable grated product rather than the cheese.
forms.animalOriginNote: Parmigiano-Reggiano DOP must be set with calf rennet, so it is not vegetarian. The production standard leaves the producer no choice.
